text:
elaine: heads-up — built a small Go CLI that sends Basic auth to Redwood. CI (GH Actions) injects the API key at build time via -ldflags. Works locally but CI binary gets 401s. anyone run into ldflags/newline issues?

 tom: usually a newline bite — echo in runner added \n. can you print the header client sends or the base64? try `echo -n` vs `echo` first :thinking: 

 elaine: curl -v from CI shows `Authorization: Basic QUxBQkE6` (redacted) but server 401s. i re-built locally with env var and it's fine. suspect secret had trailing newline from GH secret input.

 kevin: yep. common quick-check: run `echo -n "$API_KEY:" | base64` and compare to `echo "$API_KEY:" | base64` — first has no trailing A... (no newline). Example:

 ```
 $ API_KEY=abc123
 $ echo -n "$API_KEY:" | base64
 YWJjMTIzOg==
 $ echo "$API_KEY:" | base64
 YWJjMTIzOgoK
 ```

 kevin: the extra `Cg==` at the end is a newline. when the server decodes it, creds don't match.

 tom: also watch how GH Actions exposes secrets into run commands — if you do `-ldflags "-X main.apiKey=$SECRET"` the shell may add a newline. prefer `-ldflags "-X 'main.apiKey=$(printf "%s" "$SECRET")'"` or better: write secret to a file at build time and embed with `-X 'main.apiKey=@/tmp/keyfile'` pattern (if your build supports it) or pass key at runtime via env.

 elaine: thanks — fixed by switching to `printf` in the build step. CI step now:

 ```
 - name: build
   run: |
     SECRET=$(printf "%s" "$MY_SECRET")
     go build -ldflags "-X main.apiKey=$SECRET" -o app ./cmd
 ```

 elaine: 🚀 tests and prod call succeed now. leaving note: if you see Basic auth 401 only on CI, check for newline/BOM and echo -n vs echo.

 devex-bot: Related doc: https://internal.redwood.dev/devex/auth-troubleshooting (link)
